subject: Accounting
title: Reading Retained Earnings
description: A 60-second lesson on Reading Retained Earnings.

hook.text: A company has been profitable for twenty years but retained earnings are near zero. What happened?

buildup.text: Retained earnings accumulate every dollar of profit kept in the business since day one.

discovery.text: They shrink when dividends are paid or when the company posts losses.

twist.text: Some companies deliberately keep retained earnings low by returning cash to shareholders.

climax.text: Negative retained earnings signal a company has lost more money over its life than it's earned.

punchline.text: Retained earnings are the company's lifetime report card.

details.summary: Retained earnings represent the cumulative net profits a company has earned but not distributed as dividends. This topic explains how retained earnings accumulate on the balance sheet, what they signal about a company's reinvestment strategy, and their role in equity.
details.whyItMatters: Retained earnings reveal decades of accumulated profitability and capital allocation decisions. A large retained earnings balance means the company has consistently earned and reinvested more than it's paid out.
takeaways: Retained earnings equal the sum of all net income since inception minus all dividends ever paid
They appear in the equity section of the balance sheet and represent self-funded growth
Negative retained earnings (accumulated deficit) means the company has lost more than it has earned over its lifetime

faq.question: What are retained earnings?
faq.answer: Retained earnings are the total net profits a company has accumulated over its entire life minus all dividends paid to shareholders. They represent profits reinvested back into the business rather than distributed, and they appear in the shareholders' equity section of the balance sheet.

faq.question: What does an accumulated deficit mean?
faq.answer: An accumulated deficit means the company has cumulative net losses exceeding its cumulative net profits over its entire history. Many startups have accumulated deficits. Amazon had one for years before becoming profitable enough to reverse it. It doesn't necessarily mean the company is failing.
